plan: PRICE-GATED STARTER. Do not chase at 113p (two days past a print the market rejected, -7.8% on 4x volume, still making session lows). Entry band 95-105p. Tranche 1: 0.25% of $3.3M = $8.25k at <=105p. Tranche 2: 0.25% = $8.25k at <=95p. HARD CAP 0.50% ($16.5k), deliberately below the 0.75% UK band cap, until the late-Jan-2027 trading update confirms UK headcount stopped shrinking. Fills inside one session at $54k/day (20% of $271k median ADV). Friction ~59bp all-in (0.5% SDRT + 9bp half-touch).
catalyst: FY2026 trading update ~late Jan 2027 (pattern-inferred from the 28-Jan-2026 update, not company-confirmed) = the H2 read on whether the North America headcount ramp converted to revenue/margin and whether UK headcount stabilised. Then FY2026 prelims ~mid-Mar 2027 with the final dividend decision. NO FIREABLE CATALYST FOR ~6 MONTHS - dead money, docked in the score.
kill_triggers: UK Consultants assigned at year-end 2026 < 800 (from 839) - the region carrying 104% of group operating profit is still melting; exit regardless of price
Group Consultant utilisation < 91% at any reported period - the managed metric has never broken (92.8/92.9/92.7/93.6); breaking it is the AI-substitution tell
Revenue per consultant below ~£70k annualised (from ~£78-80k flat through FY24/FY25) - AI price compression arriving; cleanest quantitative AI tripwire
A third consecutive dividend cut at the FY2026 final - board no longer defends 1.27x adjusted cover
North America segment operating margin still <2% at FY2026 - the ramp was mix erosion, not a J-curve
Any drawing of debt, or cash below £22M (from £31.1M)

freezable_call.bar: UK Consultants assigned to clients at year-end 2026 >= 839 (UK headcount stops falling)
freezable_call.reasoning: UK fell three consecutive periods (1,013 -> 910 -> 839; -10.2% then -7.8%). Decisive tell: UK coaching completions FLAT at 124 (vs 130 prior year) while North America tripled to 282 - FDM is not building UK supply, so it is not expecting a UK recovery in H2.

edge_explainer: FDM published H1-2026 on 3 Aug 2026, the day before this court - the shelf row was built on FY2025 and was 7 months stale, so the print risk is BEHIND us and this is the freshest name in the band. The screen's two headline cheapness metrics do not survive primary verification: the 16.5% FCF yield is a working-capital-release artifact (FY25 CFO £20.8M was flattered by a £5.9M one-off receivables release as revenue fell; post-lease TTM FCF is £7.7M = 6.2%), and the 8.7% trailing dividend yield was halved the day before this court (interim DPS cut 3.0p from 6.0p; forward 4.4-6.2%). EV/EBIT is real and reconciles exactly to the filer (9.2x ex-lease TTM, was 8.2x on FY25). Net cash is BETTER than screened: £31.1M cash and ZERO borrowings = 25.0% of cap ex-lease, vs the screen's +11.9% which wrongly netted £19.1M of IFRS-16 leases as debt. Pension verified by hand: NO DB scheme, defined contribution only (£117k payable) - the £699k 'pension' proxy is lease dilapidations. No capital commitments (TTM capex £226k, asset-light). THE THESIS FORK: the brief's derailment test (falling headcount + falling utilisation) does NOT trigger - group headcount rose 1.9% sequentially, the first increase since 2023, utilisation hit a four-year high of 93.6%, coaching completions +50% and new client wins are accelerating. BUT the turn is in the regions that do not earn. The UK is 104% of group operating profit (10.8% margin) and is the ONE region still contracting: headcount -7.8% (1,013->910->839), revenue -5% sequentially. North America added 93 heads at a 1.4% margin and APAC 22 at -1.3%. At those unit economics the +39 net heads are worth about -£0.3M of half-year profit. Counter-argument that must be held open: NA margin is depressed BY the ramp (coaching cost lands now, billings run for years) and NA was a £92.2M business in FY2024 vs £45.8M in FY2025, so a genuine J-curve is possible; one half cannot settle it. AI CONFLICT vs the frozen house call AI-BREAK|2027-12-31 @ 0.45: FDM has two opposing exposures and they must not be averaged. It is SHORT AI-substitution (more AI = fewer entry-level bodies; a break deflates the terminal-value fear and the multiple re-rates) but LONG enterprise IT budgets (its clients are banks and insurers, it now sells 'AI-enabled talent', and 10% of 2026 executive bonus is tied to consultants deployed on AI projects, so a capex break freezes the budgets it sells into). The entry does NOT require the AI cycle holding, and FDM is one of very few names in the book whose first-order channel is HELPED by a break - real diversification value against a household already carrying ~$5.2M / 26% AI-complex exposure - but it is NOT a hedge and must not be sized as insurance. Critically, substitution is NOT yet visible in the two metrics that would show it: utilisation never fell (92.8/92.9/92.7/93.6) and revenue per consultant is flat at ~£78-80k. The collapse began in 2023 with the rate shock and is concentrated in North America (-50%) and EMEA (-32%) against a UK down only 15% - a geographic signature that looks like a US bank capex cycle, not a technology. The sharpest observation available: FDM already lived through the 'AI adoption continues' scenario and it cost 76% of EBIT, because record enterprise tech spending went to AI infrastructure rather than to people. Is the substitution priced? EV £93.2M against peak adjusted EBIT £55.0M = 1.7x peak, so heavy permanent impairment IS priced; against TTM adjusted EBIT £10.1M it is 9.2x, pricing essentially zero recovery. RULING: derailment, not de-rate - revenue -19%, PBT -49%, EPS -51% and the dividend -50% are all still negative year-on-year, and the de-rate pattern requires stable-or-rising estimates. What stops it being terminal is that the leading metrics inflected while the lagging ones have not, plus a pristine verified balance sheet. Trough anchor fires: EBIT 0.243x its FY2023 peak of £55.0M = MELTING by the house rule; honestly it is BOTH normalisation of a real post-COVID bank-tech hiring bubble AND operating deleverage (revenue halved, EBIT -76%). Dividend honesty: rebased twice (22.5p -> 10.0p -> 3.0p interim); FY2025 cover was 0.52x on statutory EPS so the old payout was genuinely unsustainable and the board cut rather than fund it from the balance sheet - the honest pattern, not the value-trap pattern. Honesty grade REVIEW_FLAG not ELEVATE: management leads on a favourable group aggregate that masks adverse regional mix, but prints full regional headcount AND segment profit on the same pages, took the EMEA goodwill write-off in full, escalated the AI risk in its own risk register, and cut the dividend 50% in the same announcement - nothing concealed. E[FV] 124p vs 113.3p = +9.4pp, thin against a -38% bear, so the position is price-gated to 95-105p and capped at 0.50%.
